chunks: And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said:
"Nothing has effaced Islam as anything has effaced it like miserliness."
Then he said: "Indeed, this miserliness has a creeping like the creeping of ants, and branches like the branches of a net."

key_terms.الشَّرَكِ: a net or snare with interwoven strands
key_terms.الشُّحِّ: miserliness or greedy stinginess rooted in the soul
key_terms.النَّمْلِ: ants, used here as an image of quiet, hidden movement
key_terms.الْإِسْلَامَ: Islam, the religion and way of submission to Allah
key_terms.دَبِيبًا: a creeping, subtle movement or infiltration

ai.seo_question: How does the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم describe the danger of miserliness in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith warns that shuhh, a deep selfish miserliness, is among the most destructive moral diseases for the Muslim community. It portrays this vice as subtle and pervasive, entering gradually and spreading into many harmful forms.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1716 - The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said:
"Nothing has eroded Islam as much as miserliness (shuhh)."

He then added:
"This miserliness creeps in like the creeping of ants and has branches like the branches of a net."
